subject: POC trial planning - ACME Software
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anika Sharma <anika@acme-software.com>, Ben Turner <ben.turner@acme-software.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: POC trial planning - ACME Software

Thanks again for the call today — great alignment on goals. As promised, a quick recap of the proposed POC/trial plan and next steps so we can lock the kickoff. Please confirm or flag any edits.

Summary & success criteria (proposed)
- Primary success metric: 95th percentile generation latency <= 300ms for typical 512-token requests in our test harness.
- Accuracy/quality: mean task success rate >= 85% on ACME's evaluation prompts (see attached).
- Cost: token cost per 1k tokens within agreed threshold (we can iterate during POC).

Evaluation plan
- Redwood provides a dedicated trial instance (shared pilot) and one SE for onboarding.
- ACME provides sample prompts, representative dataset, and target SLAs.
- Weekly evaluation checkpoints with a short quality readout; final readout at the end of the trial.

Timeline & milestones (proposed)
- Kickoff: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 — intro, environment access, initial workload baseline.
- Week 1: Ingest sample dataset, baseline runs, initial latency tuning.
- Week 2-3: Model/config tuning, caching/batching experiments, early quality checks.
- Weekly check-ins: Tuesdays 10:00 AM PT (proposed).
- Final readout: 20 Mar 2026 — full results and recommendation.

Ownership & next steps
- ACME: confirm technical owner and dataset/access plan (Ben?).
- Redwood: SE support (Dylan), AM coordination (Marissa), and SRE for infra as needed.
- Action: Please confirm success criteria and proposed kickoff time. I attached the Redwood POC template and a draft success-criteria workbook.

Attachments:
- Redwood-POC-template.pdf (application/pdf)
- POC-success-criteria.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com

From: Anika Sharma <anika@acme-software.com>

Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:24:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC trial planning - ACME Software

Marissa — thanks for the thorough recap. This looks good and close to what we discussed. A few notes from our side: 

1) Success criteria tweak: For quality we'd like two metrics — (a) task success rate >= 85% on our eval set, and (b) no more than 5% hallucination rate on NER/extraction tasks. Can Redwood help run the hallucination check?
2) Technical owner: Ben will be our primary technical contact and will handle dataset access. Ben, can you confirm timelines for providing the eval prompts/dataset?
3) SE: We would like a dedicated SE during the first two weeks for onboarding — helps speed tuning.
4) Compliance: Please share the SOC2 summary and any FedRAMP guidance you have; our security team will start a quick review.

I've attached our initial evaluation questions and a sample prompt pack. Let's aim to confirm kickoff time by EOD tomorrow.

Attachments:
- ACME-eval-questions.docx (document)

Thanks,
Anika Sharma
Head of ML Platform | ACME Software
anika@acme-software.com

Hi all — Dylan here (SE). Happy to run the hallucination checks and help instrument the eval harness. I can be dedicated for onboarding for the first two weeks as requested.

Quick asks from my side before kickoff:
- Can Ben provide a sample of the eval prompts and a small dataset (S3 link preferred) and test credentials?
- Do you have an internal success-metric dashboard or should we share our lightweight QA dashboard (we can link to a read-only view)?

Proposed weekly check-in cadence: Tuesdays 11:00 AM PT (works better for my schedule).

I’ll prepare an initial checklist for kickoff (access, test prompts, baseline runs, monitoring hooks) and share it ahead of the meeting.

- Kickoff: Tue, 24 Feb 2026, 10:00 AM PT — 60min (calendar invite: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=acme-poc-kickoff-20260224)
- Weekly check-ins: Tuesdays 11:00 AM PT (Dylan to lead technical check-ins)
